title: Soft-Body Gear Press on Deformable ShaderBall
description: A jelly-like ShaderBall2 sits on a platform while a set of interlocking gears hovers above it. The user clicks to lower the spinning gears into the ShaderBall, causing it to visibly squish and deform in real time. The user can adjust gear speed, press depth, and release the gears to watch the ball elastically recover its shape.
prompt: Create a single HTML file using Three.js r170 that implements a soft-body gear press simulation. Load both 'shared_assets/gears.glb' and 'shared_assets/ShaderBall2.glb' using GLTFLoader. Place the ShaderBall2 at the center of the scene on a flat ground plane, scaled so it is roughly 2 units in diameter. Position the gears assembly directly above the ShaderBall2, rotated so the gear teeth face downward. Use a perspective camera at position (0, 3, 6) looking at the origin, with OrbitControls for rotation only (no pan or zoom). Add a directional light from upper-right, a hemisphere light for ambient fill, and a subtle environment map or tone mapping for realism. Implement a vertex-based soft-body deformation on the ShaderBall2 mesh: store original vertex positions, and when the gears descend, displace vertices downward and outward proportionally to their proximity to the gear contact surface using a radial falloff function. Add elastic spring-back by interpolating displaced vertices back toward their rest positions each frame with a damping factor of 0.04. The gears should continuously rotate around their shared axis at a base speed. Provide these interactions: (1) A 'Press' button that animates the gears downward over 1 second using a smooth ease-in-out tween until they penetrate the top 30% of the ShaderBall2, triggering deformation. (2) A 'Release' button that raises the gears back up and lets the ball recover elastically over 2 seconds. (3) A slider labeled 'Gear Speed' (range 0.5 to 5.0) controlling gear rotation speed. (4) A slider labeled 'Press Depth' (range 0.2 to 0.8) controlling how far the gears descend into the ball. (5) A 'Reset' button that restores all vertices to original positions and resets gear height. Use a simple UI overlay with HTML elements positioned at top-left. The ShaderBall2 material should use a glossy, slightly translucent appearance to suggest jelly-like softness. Ensure the deformation updates every frame in the animation loop by modifying geometry attributes and setting needsUpdate flags.
